name: MITNICK, Kevin
affiliations: Mitnick Security Consulting; KnowBe4 (Chief Hacking Officer)
description: Once the most-wanted computer criminal in the United States; arrested by the FBI in 1995 after a high-profile pursuit and convicted of wire fraud and unauthorized access. Pioneered social-engineering tradecraft against telecom and tech firms. After release he became a celebrated white-hat consultant, author and speaker. Died of pancreatic cancer in July 2023.

name: POULSEN, Kevin
description: Notorious for seizing the phone lines of an LA radio station in 1990 to guarantee himself a winning call and claim a Porsche. Served prison time for hacking and wire fraud. Reinvented as an investigative journalist, co-authored the SecureDrop whistleblower platform, and reported extensively on cybercrime.

name: LAMO, Adrian
description: Known for intrusions into The New York Times and Microsoft networks, often working from libraries and cafes. In 2010 he reported U.S. Army analyst Chelsea Manning to authorities over the WikiLeaks disclosures, a decision that drew lasting controversy. Died in 2018 at age 37.

name: McKINNON, Gary
description: Scottish systems administrator accused of the largest-ever intrusion into U.S. military and NASA computers (2001–2002), reportedly searching for suppressed evidence of UFOs and free-energy technology. A decade-long extradition fight ended in 2012 when the UK Home Secretary blocked his removal on human-rights grounds, citing his Asperger's diagnosis.

name: GONZALEZ, Albert
affiliations: ShadowCrew · Operation Get Rich or Die Tryin'
description: Mastermind behind the theft of more than 170 million card and ATM numbers from TJX, Heartland Payment Systems and others — among the largest data breaches on record. Operated partly as a paid Secret Service informant while continuing to run his own crews. Sentenced in 2010 to 20 years in federal prison.

name: JAMES, Jonathan
description: As a teenager, breached the U.S. Department of Defense and NASA systems, intercepting thousands of messages and source code for the International Space Station's life-support software. In 2000 became the first juvenile incarcerated for cybercrime in the United States. Died in 2008 amid an investigation he denied involvement in.

name: MORRIS, Robert Tappan
description: Author of the 1988 Morris Worm, the first major worm to spread across the early internet and the first felony conviction under the U.S. Computer Fraud and Abuse Act. Now a tenured professor at MIT and co-founder of Viaweb and the startup accelerator Y Combinator. A respected figure in computer-science research.

name: CALCE, Michael
description: At 15, launched a wave of distributed denial-of-service attacks in February 2000 that took down Yahoo, Amazon, eBay, CNN and Dell, briefly crippling some of the web's largest sites. Sentenced in juvenile court in Canada. Now works as a white-hat consultant and author on cybersecurity awareness.

name: HUTCHINS, Marcus
description: Registered the kill-switch domain that halted the global WannaCry ransomware outbreak in May 2017, sparing untold systems including the UK's NHS. Later arrested in the U.S. and pleaded guilty to earlier involvement in the Kronos banking trojan; sentenced to time served. Continues to publish respected malware-analysis research.

name: ZATKO, Peiter
description: Leading member of the L0pht hacker think-tank who famously testified to the U.S. Senate in 1998 that the group could take down the internet in 30 minutes. Went on to run cyber programs at DARPA and lead security at Google, Stripe and Twitter. In 2022 became a high-profile whistleblower over Twitter's security practices.
